summary: עשׂר is the number ten and what is counted by it. עֶשֶׂר/עֲשָׂרָה is ten, עָשָׂר/עֶשְׂרֵה the “-teen” of eleven to nineteen (the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Lev 23:5–6, 34), עֶשְׂרִים twenty; עָשׂוֹר is a ten, and above all the tenth day of a month (Lev 23:27), עֲשִׂירִי the tenth. A tenth part is the עִשָּׂרוֹן of fine flour with the offerings (Lev 23:13, 17) and the מַעֲשֵׂר, the tenth of produce and flock that is holy to Yahweh (Lev 27:30–32), which Abraham gave to Melchizedek (Gen 14:20; Heb 7:4); the verb is to take or give that tenth. Arabic, Ugaritic and Akkadian have the same root for ten, tenth, twenty and tithe, and Arabic and Ugaritic show an ʿ behind its ע.

words.summary: The form of ten that joins a unit to make eleven to nineteen, masculine עָשָׂר and feminine עֶשְׂרֵה, as cardinal and as ordinal of the days of a month.

doctrine.statement: “All the tithe of the land … is Yahweh’s; it is holy to Yahweh” (Lev 27:30, 32). Yahweh gives it to the Levites for their inheritance, because they have no portion in the land (Num 18:21, 24), and they in turn give a tenth of it to him (Num 18:26). Every third year it feeds the Levite, the sojourner, the fatherless and the widow, “that Yahweh your God may bless you” (Deu 14:28–29), and eaten before him it teaches Israel “to fear Yahweh your God always” (Deu 14:23). When Israel asks for a king like the nations, Samuel warns that the king will take the tenth (יַעְשֹׂר) of their seed and flocks for his servants, and Yahweh says, “they have rejected me” (1Sa 8:7, 15, 17). Withholding it is robbing God (Mal 3:8–10). Yet the tithe is not the whole of what is owed: Jesus tells those who tithe mint and dill and cumin that they have left the weightier things of the Law, justice, mercy and faithfulness, which they ought to have done without leaving the other undone (Mat 23:23); the Pharisee who tithes all he gets goes home not justified, the tax collector who asks for mercy justified (Luk 18:12–14).

Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth of everything (Gen 14:18–20). Yahweh swears to David’s Lord, “You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek” (Psa 110:4). Hebrews reads the tenth as the proof of that order’s greatness: Abraham the patriarch gave him a tenth of the spoils; the sons of Levi take tithes from their brothers by the Law, but Melchizedek, not of their descent, took a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises, and the lesser is blessed by the greater; here men who die receive tithes, there one of whom it is witnessed that he lives; and Levi himself, who receives tithes, paid a tenth through Abraham, being still in his father’s loins (Heb 7:1–10). From this Hebrews argues that perfection was not through the Levitical priesthood, and that Jesus, of Judah, is priest “by the power of an endless life” (Heb 7:11–17).

note: Left out: the name עַשְׁוָת Ashvath (BDB p.gb.al, 1Ch 7:33), spelled with ש, for a name entry; BDB m.da.at מַעֲשֵׂר is a redirect with no tokens. The root עשׁר “be rich” (עָשַׁר, עֹשֶׁר, עָשִׁיר, BDB p.ge.*) is shin, not sin, and a separate root key; Aramaic and Syriac show it with ת (ʿtr, Syriac ܥܘܬܪܐ), i.e. older ṯ, so it is not this root. Ugaritic has a second ʿšr “feast, give a banquet” (Segert p. 197, KTU 1.17 VI 30, compared with Ge’ez ʿaššara “invite”, ʿašur “banquet”), which Segert offers as a possible reading of ʿšrt in KTU 1.119:32; no Hebrew word shows it, so it is not recorded as a cognate. Arabic عشر also has “consort with, kinsfolk” (عَاشَرَ, عَشِيرَة, Lane pp. 2051–2053), which Lane links to the number only for مَعْشَر; not recorded, since no Hebrew word shares it. Not consulted: Ge’ez ʿaśartu, ʿəśrā (Dillmann, Leslau; Wiktionary lead only), Phoenician ʿšr (Krahmalkov), Sabaic. Segert p. 197 checked on the page image (archive.org leaf n224). The Lev 23 forms: v5 בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר, v6/34/39 בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר (עָשָׂר); v27 בֶּעָשׂוֹר; v13/17 שְׁנֵי עֶשְׂרֹנִים (עִשָּׂרוֹן). Open: (1) whether the tenth day of the seventh month (יוֹם הַכִּפֻּרִים) and of the first month (the lamb taken, Exo 12:3) carry a doctrine through the number itself; nothing in scripture draws on “tenth” there, so none is written (covering belongs to כפר). (2) The qal of 1Sa 8:15, 17 is the king’s taking a tenth; it is kin to the tithe but names only the word-level cognates. (3) Syriac lemma pointings (עֲסַר, עֶסְרִין, מַעְסְרָא, עַסַּר) follow SEDRA’s forms; check the stems (SEDRA lists Mat 23:23 מְעַסְּרִין as pael participle and Heb 7:9 אֶתְעַסַּר).
